cases.title: @file: with JMESPath selectors, an env placeholder in the path, and nested @file resolution
cases.intent: Merged with CORE-CFG-FILE-SELECTOR-01. @file:<path>@<selector> loads a JSON file and keeps only what the JMESPath selector selects (IncludeResolver.kt:67-69, :83-91); its path is placeholder-substituted first (:61), so ${SFC_E2E_CASE_DIR} works here although it does not in @include (CORE-CFG-INCLUDE-ENV-01). A string inside loaded content is itself resolved (JsonHelper.kt:276): the ctr channel's Simulation is a second @file. Three sections are built this way: Transformations (selector xf), the schedule's Metadata (selector meta, beside a decoy 'other') and the channels (selector channels, beside a decoy 'unused'). @file stays out of AdapterTypes/TargetTypes/ProtocolAdapters/Targets, so all modes apply.

assert.comment: Counter from sim.json, a nested @file inside shared.json
Constant 10 through Plus1, a transformation loaded with the xf selector
the 'unused' decoy beside the selected node is not included
schedule Metadata from the meta selector, not 'other'

cases.title: An @file selector that selects nothing is reported precisely, then sfc-main idles (known defect)
cases.intent: Split from CORE-CFG-FILE-SELECT-01 (its negative sub-run). A JMESPath selector that returns nothing raises 'Selector "nope" ... is invalid or returns no selected data' (IncludeResolver.kt:85-89) rather than silently including null. The message names the selector and the include string, which is what an operator needs. The IncludeResolverException then lands in the provider-loop swallow.

wait.comment: Liveness: the claim is that sfc-main does NOT exit after logging the error. Absence of an exit has no event to wait on, so the case gives it 3 s and the exit code then shows who ended the process (143 = stopped by the harness, 0/1 = exited by itself).

assert.text: shared.json@nope" is invalid or returns no selected data

knownDefect.summary: The selector IncludeResolverException is thrown inside ConfigFileProvider's provider loop and only logged (ConfigFileProvider.kt:142-147), so no configuration is ever emitted and ServiceMain waits forever (ServiceMain.kt:100-102): an idle process with no exit code, which a supervisor sees as healthy. Correct: exit 1, as configuration validation errors do (ServiceMain.kt:171-173).

cases.title: @include in key form (raw fragment) and value form, nested, with placeholders inside included text
cases.intent: @include is a textual include on the raw configuration, before JSON parsing (ConfigReader.kt:70). The key form "@include": "file" splices the file's text in place of the whole member, including a trailing comma (the regex at ConfigReader.kt:172 consumes it, so a fragment that is followed by more members must end with its own comma). The value form "@include:file" replaces a value and consumes a trailing comma the same way, so it is used as the last member of its object (the IPC transform appends AdapterServers/TargetServers at the top level). Here the Schedules come from a top-level key-form include, the sim source from a value-form include, whose file itself includes the Counter channel, and Metadata from a key-form include that nests a second one carrying an env placeholder, which is substituted after inclusion (:88-89). Relative include paths resolve against the process working directory (ConfigReader.kt:234), which the harness sets to the unit directory; the case files are copied to its case/ subdirectory, so includes are written as case/<file>.

assert.comment: ctr comes from channels.txt, included inside the value-form include
the schedule comes from the top-level key-form include

cases.title: @include fails in compact single-line JSON because the include regex is line-greedy (known defect)
cases.intent: The include regex captures the file name with a greedy (.*) up to the last quote on the line (ConfigReader.kt:172). With one member per line that is the closing quote of the path; in compact single-line JSON - generated configurations, SFC_CONFIG values - it swallows the rest of the document, so the include looks for a file named 'case/meta.txt"},...' and fails. The case runs the minified configuration from the case directory (uberjar only: the harness does not render that fixture).

Correct: match the quoted path non-greedily, and the records carry the included tag.

cases.title: Relative @include paths resolve against the process working directory, not the configuration file's directory
cases.intent: ConfigReader opens included files with File(name) (ConfigReader.kt:234), so a relative path resolves against the working directory; that is undocumented, and a move to config-relative paths would silently change which file is read. The case runs sfc-main on conf/main.json inside the case directory, while the working directory is the unit directory. main.json includes case/meta.txt, and both candidate files exist with different tags: <cwd>/case/meta.txt and <config dir>/case/meta.txt. Every record shows which one was read. Uberjar only: -config points at a fixture the harness does not render, which would need JarFiles in-process.

cases.title: A circular @include is detected and reported, but leaves sfc-main idle (known defect)
cases.intent: a.txt includes b.txt, which includes a.txt. includeFiles keeps a trail of absolute paths and throws 'Recursive inclusion found for file' when a file reappears (ConfigReader.kt:238-240); without that check the textual expansion would never terminate. Detection works, but the exception lands in the same provider-loop swallow as every include error, so the process neither runs nor exits.

cases.title: An @file include that loads itself is detected as recursion, but leaves sfc-main idle (known defect)
cases.intent: Split from CORE-CFG-INCLUDE-CYCLE-01: @file: is resolved on the parsed JSON by IncludeResolver, a different mechanism from @include, with its own trail. A string inside loaded content is resolved again with the loading file on the trail (JsonHelper.kt:276), so shared.json referencing itself must raise 'Recursion processing included file' (IncludeResolver.kt:106-107). The IncludeResolverException is logged as 'Error resolving configuration' (ConfigFileProvider.kt:143-144) and the process idles.

cases.title: An environment placeholder in an @include path is not substituted, and the include error stalls SFC (known defect)
cases.intent: includeFiles runs on the raw text before any placeholder substitution (ConfigReader.kt:70 versus :88-89), unlike @file:, whose path is substituted first (IncludeResolver.kt:61, see CORE-CFG-FILE-SELECT-01). The include therefore looks for a file literally named '${SFC_E2E_CASE_DIR}/meta.txt' relative to the working directory, which does not exist although the intended file does. The error then stalls sfc-main like any include error.

cases.title: Setting MonitorIncludedConfigContentInterval breaks startup whenever includes are present (known defect)
cases.intent: Merged with CORE-CFG-MONITOR-INTERVAL-01. When a configuration has includes, ConfigFileProvider reads the include-watcher settings from the raw map and casts the interval with 'as Int' (ConfigFileProvider.kt:157), but Gson parses every JSON number as a Double, so any explicit value - including 0, the documented way to switch URL polling off - throws ClassCastException. That is swallowed by the provider loop and the configuration is never emitted. The configuration is CORE-CFG-INCLUDE-01's working Metadata include plus that one key; the cast runs only when includes exist (:163-166).

assert.text: java.lang.Double cannot be cast to class java.lang.Integer

knownDefect.summary: getIncludeWatcherSettings casts the Gson-parsed Double with 'as Int' (ConfigFileProvider.kt:157), so any configured MonitorIncludedConfigContentInterval throws ClassCastException when includes exist, and the swallow at :142-147 leaves an idle process. Correct: (value as Number).toInt(); the records then carry the included tag.

cases.title: A missing @include file is reported, then sfc-main idles forever instead of exiting (known defect)
cases.intent: ConfigFileProvider resolves includes before it emits a configuration (ConfigFileProvider.kt:162 -> ConfigReader.kt:242). The ConfigurationException for the missing file is caught by the provider loop, logged as 'Error in configuration' (:142-147), and the loop goes back to waiting, so ServiceMain never receives a configuration and never exits. The case waits for the exact error, gives the process time to exit, and then reads the exit code: 143 means the harness had to stop it.
